sections.title: Opening maps
paragraphs: Click Load maps directory and choose a folder. Only images and PDFs are listed; other files are ignored. Subfolders appear as groups.
You can also drag a folder or a file into the window. A loose map opens straight in the viewer.
No folder: press V to open the empty viewer and drag a map into it, or use the Choose a map button.
In the desktop app, the last folder you loaded is reopened at startup. Everything is read on this device; nothing is uploaded.

sections.title: Searching
paragraphs: The search field looks for maps by name in all folders and shows the results right below it. Click a result to open it, or press Enter to open the first one.
The view buttons switch between grid (thumbnails) and list. With subfolders, search opens in list view, with one row per subfolder.

sections.title: Map viewer
items: Right column: lists the maps in the folder so you can switch maps with one click. Show or hide it with the button next to the navigation, or with L.
Full screen: the button fills the whole window. Esc leaves it.
Close: the X, Esc, or a click outside the window.
PDF: pages appear in sequence, up to 200 pages. When you change the zoom, the pages are redrawn sharply.

sections.title: Zoom and brightness
paragraphs: Zoom from 100% to 600%. Brightness from 50% to 150%, where 100% is the image as it is.
Adjust them with the keyboard (see the shortcuts below). The toolbar has no sliders, and the value is not shown on screen.
When zoomed past 100%, drag the image with the mouse to see other parts.

sections.title: Protractor
paragraphs: Turn it on with the protractor icon. The first click places the centre; moving the pointer aims the arrow; the second click locks the angle, which appears at the tip. 0° is north, and degrees increase clockwise.
Magnetic declination: type the declination in degrees, with its sign (for example -20 or 15). A second needle shows the corrected angle, and route bearings also show the magnetic value.
Esc removes the ring or the arrow without closing the window.

sections.title: Measure
paragraphs: Turn on the ruler icon and click to mark points. The length of each segment appears over the line. Double-click or right-click ends the measurement; Esc ends only the segment in progress.
Without a scale, the measurement is in cm on paper, using the resolution stored in the image when it exists. With the map scale, the measurement becomes a real distance.

Calibrate (only for images without a stored resolution): turn on Measure, click the crosshair icon, draw a line over something of known size, and type its real length in cm. PDFs already have an exact scale.
The trash icon clears all measurements.

sections.title: Map scale
paragraphs: Choose the map type: Aviation and Nautical measure in nautical miles (NM); Land measures in metres and kilometres. Then type the scale, for example 1:1000000.
With a scale, measurements and routes show real distances. An invalid scale is marked in red.

sections.title: Plot points and route
paragraphs: Turn on the pin icon. Each click marks a numbered point. Between points you get the route line, the bearing (above the segment) and the distance in nautical miles (below it, with a scale).
The route total appears in the bottom bar, next to the file name. The trash icon clears all points.
Correcting the track: double-click the degree above a leg, type the new bearing and press Enter. The second point of the leg moves along that bearing, keeping the distance. Esc cancels.
Renaming a point: double-click its marker, type a name (up to 8 characters) and press Enter. Esc cancels; an empty name goes back to the number.
Export route (button at the end of the bar): saves a CSV file with each leg's track, distance, wind, TAS, drift correction, true and magnetic heading and ground speed.

sections.title: Wind
paragraphs: Turn on the wind icon, then click on the map. A box opens at the point: type the direction in degrees, where the wind comes from (0 = north, as in METAR), and the speed in knots. Enter adds the arrow; Esc cancels.
The arrow points to where the wind blows to: a wind from 280° points to 100°. The speed in knots appears under the arrow. Backspace removes the last arrow; the trash icon clears all of them.

Drift correction: type the TAS (true airspeed) in the field next to the wind icon. Each route leg shows a small plane on its line. Without wind, the nose points the same way as the line between the two points. With wind and TAS, it points to the corrected heading (HDG), with the magnetic declination added (0 if none is typed). The degree appears at the nose. The calculation uses the true wind: forecast winds aloft are true (°V); tower or ATIS winds are magnetic, so press the °M button in the wind form (without a declination, 0 is used). The TAS and the wind speed can be in knots or km/h: the button next to TAS switches the unit.
Correcting a wind: double-click the arrow or its speed label. A form opens with its direction, speed, reference (°V/°M) and the TAS; press Enter to confirm or Esc to cancel.

In search: open the first result

Brighten. On a Mac, Alt is the Option key
Measure, plot or wind: remove the last point or arrow. With no segment in progress, remove the last measurement
Measure: end the segment in progress. Protractor: remove the ring or the arrow

sections.title: Mouse
items: Click: marks a point, depending on the tool on (measure, plot, wind or protractor).
Double-click or right-click: ends the measurement.
Click and drag: moves the image when it is zoomed.

sections.title: Note
items: Cmd or Ctrl with + and - still control the browser's zoom, not the image's zoom.
